prompt:
You are a sceptical financial analyst reviewing a forecast prepared by a colleague.

Given the following forecast for TCS (base year 2021):
{
  "strategy": "alt_strategy",
  "base_year": 2021,
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "forecast": [
    {
      "year": 2022,
      "revenue_cr": 191486,
      "net_income_cr": 38900,
      "eps": 104.0
    },
    {
      "year": 2023,
      "revenue_cr": 216679,
      "net_income_cr": 44200,
      "eps": 118.2
    },
    {
      "year": 2024,
      "revenue_cr": 240714,
      "net_income_cr": 49100,
      "eps": 131.3
    }
  ],
  "top_assumptions": [
    "Post-pandemic demand recovery drives constant-currency growth rebounding to ~7-8% in FY2022 and normalising toward the pre-pandemic 3-year CAGR of ~8-9% in INR terms, as Q1 FY2021 pandemic drag fully rolls off and digital transformation spending accelerates across BFSI, CMT, and Retail verticals.",
    "Net profit margin stabilises at ~20-21% of revenues (consistent with the FY2020-21 reported adjusted margin of ~20.3%), with the one-off legal claim provision of INR 1,218 crore from FY2021 not recurring, partially offset by continued employee cost pressure from wage hikes and headcount addition in a tight talent market."
  ],
  "reasoning": "FY2021 is anomalous: reported INR revenue growth was 4.6% but constant-currency growth was -0.8% due to the COVID-19 pandemic sharply depressing Q1 FY2021 revenues across all verticals; the prior year (FY2020) showed 7.2% INR growth and ~7% constant-currency growth. Accordingly, the latest year-on-year growth rate is not a reliable projection basis. The 3-5 year pre-pandemic CAGR for TCS was approximately 8-10% in INR terms; blending recovery mean-reversion (base effect from weak Q1 FY2021 lapping off) with this CAGR, a ~16-17% INR revenue growth is assumed for FY2022 (reflecting both real demand recovery and favourable base), moderating to ~13% in FY2023 and ~11% in FY2024 as growth normalises. The exceptional legal provision (INR 1,218 crore) is treated as non-recurring, supporting margin improvement in FY2022 and beyond. The balance sheet is debt-light with strong free cash flow generation (~INR 38,802 crore OCF in FY2021), capex modest at ~INR 2,719 crore, confirming no financial constraint on growth execution."
}

Step 1: Identify the 3 most critical assumptions embedded in this forecast.
Step 2: For each assumption, describe one plausible scenario where it fails.
Step 3: Rate each assumption failure as Low / Medium / High risk to the forecast accuracy.
Step 4: Assign an overall confidence score from 0-100 (100 = completely certain).

RESPONSE FORMAT: Begin your response DIRECTLY with the opening brace { — no reasoning or text before the JSON.

Return ONLY valid JSON:
{
  "company": "<COMPANY>",
  "base_year": <YYYY>,
  "strategy": "<baseline|alt_strategy>",
  "assumptions": [
    {"assumption": "<text>", "failure_scenario": "<text>", "risk": "<Low|Medium|High>"}
  ],
  "confidence_score": <0-100>,
  "overall_critique": "<2 sentences>"
}
